utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Patricia Sellers from the Office of the Prosecutor. With me today with co-counsels, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager is Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. Good morning to our colleagues on the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Sellers, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones we represent Mr. Naser Oric. And we have our legal assistant with us, Ms. Adisa Mehic and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries? None.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a piece of information that we have succeeded in moving the sittings of the 27th and 29th of September from the afternoon to the morning, and we would be sitting in Courtroom III, this courtroom. However, we have not yet succeeded in moving the sitting of the 28th. There may be a slight chance of moving it. I can't promise it. What I can promise is that we will keep working on it. So let's bring in the witness. I take it, Ms. Sellers, that you anticipate to finish?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I anticipate finishing possibly towards the end of the second session and at very most --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take your time. I mean, it's -- we have a whole day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are continuing with the cross-examination this morning. You're still testifying pursuant to your solemn declaration, and we hope to be able to finish with your cross-examination today, after which there may be re-examination and possibly some questions from the Bench. And you will then be free to go home. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Sellers: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tiro. I'm going to continue asking questions of you today, and as we discussed yesterday please confine your answer to the subject matter when yes or no is appropriate or if a longer explanation is appropriate please give that type of answer. I just wanted to finish up very briefly with any knowledge you had concerning the humanitarian aid. We talked about how the aid was given to the civilians who needed food. I'd like to ask you: To your knowledge was any of the humanitarian aid given to fighters who were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which fighters were there. If a person wasn't in uniform and I didn't see them with a rifle, I couldn't tell whether they were a soldier or a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any persons in Srebrenica in uniform?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see any in uniform in 1992. I don't know where they would get a uniform from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw persons in Srebrenica in uniform in 1993. Would that be your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he there in 1993? Because if I remember well -- when did he leave Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my impression is in 1993 he was there, and I believe Mr. Tiro testified that he then became a member of a unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ejub Golic's unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tiro, then you saw only persons in uniform in 1993. Is that your testimony so I can be clear?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I would like to ask you then: Were you aware of any canteen where soldiers or fighters would eat or be served food in 1992 or in 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Always in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In Srebrenica, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was just a kitchen or a canteen for civilians, for the infirm. And I could show you where this kitchen was set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where the kitchen was set up in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the department store, across from the -- the street from the department store.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see persons eating at that canteen in 1993 who were in uniform?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that canteen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may react. The witness said that in 1993 he went to Cizmici and that is not quite Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But when did he return to Srebrenica to join Ejub Golic's unit? If it was in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we clarify. Were you in Srebrenica in 1993, in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm asking this, Ms. Sellers, because I get the impression that in 1992 he was there from July to December and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would then like to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I would like to know exactly if he did return to Srebrenica, when he returned to Srebrenica. I think we need to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At least it's not clear in my mind. I may have missed something, but it's not clear in my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, can you tell us whether you were in Srebrenica in 1993, January.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I was -- actually later when I found the rifle I was in Cizmici and that is in the Bratunac municipality. My family was in Srebrenica, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were not in Srebrenica in 1993. That's what we're just trying to clarify. You were -- as of 1993, you were always in Cizmici and the Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we should only discuss your physical being in Srebrenica in 1992, if I understand correctly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were just saying that the canteen was located in front of the department store. Would I also be correct in assuming that in 1992 you did not eat in the canteen?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not. This was for the elderly and the infirm. Those who didn't have anyone to cook for them or to bring food for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the canteen was able to provide food for the persons, the elderly and the infirm, who did come there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The kitchen was opened only after the convoys entered Srebrenica. When the convoy arrived, that's when the kitchen was formed. It wasn't there before the convoys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Golic [sic], you testified that you joined the unit of a man named Ejub Golic in 1993. You said in your testimony, in your evidence, that you voluntarily joined the unit and you could have chosen to join any other units but you joined Mr. Golic's unit. I would like to ask you first: Had you heard of Ejub Golic in 1992 while you were in Srebrenica or did you know him before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I heard of him as a civilian before the war, but I didn't hear about him forming a unit in the course of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understood that the witness answered -- actually that was the whole point of my objection. He said something else. He said he meant -- he joined the group of people with Ejub Golic; he didn't mention any unit. And this is all that I wanted to clarify regarding the -- what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please put the question whether it was a group or a unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, could you just give me one minute, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If necessary, go to yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, I wouldn't know which part of the transcript it is, but if you need a short break to go locate it --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can assist. That's on page 49, lines 1 to line 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yesterday was the 6th, wasn't it? So let's go here. I will read because we need to clarify this if it's being contested because we need to clarify it now. "Q. Now I would like to ask you something else." I'm reading from page 49 of yesterday's transcript, line 5. "Q. Now I would like to ask you something else. At the time when you were in Kravica you found a rifle there. Did there come a time that you joined a unit?" This is what we have in the transcript. "A. Yes. A group of armed soldiers, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "Q. Which group? "A. I joined the Cizmici with Ejub Golic. "Q. Why? "A. Well, out of my own free will. "Q. Yes, you decided that, but why did you decide to join Ejub Golic. "A. Because I knew that man from before. "Q. I would like to ask you this: How long did you spend in Ejub Golic's group; do you remember? "A. I spent a long time with Ejub Golic defending Cizmici. "Q. During the time you were in that group, did you have contacts with Mr. Ejub Golic, did you have personal contacts with him? "A. Yes. "Q. Did you have several contacts with him or not? "A. Yes. We were in touch on several occasions."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then you continue -- tell us -- "do you have any information about whether Mr. Ejub Golic and that group of people around him considered anybody in Srebrenica as their commander? Was it stated that there was a command in Srebrenica." And he answered in the negative.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the point I was referring to, and I see Madam Vidovic on her feet, was on the following page, line 12 through line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll find it first. I'll soon come to you, Ms. Vidovic, but let's finish. Line 12 and 13. "Q. The fact that you went to Ejub Golic's unit, was that of your own free will? Were you able to go anywhere or could you please explain this to the Trial Chamber? "A. Once I found the rifle I could go to any unit. It doesn't -- doesn't matter whether it was Ejub Golic's group or any other group. I went to his group because he was -- he is from my municipality and Cizmici were the only ones that remained in the Bratunac municipality." Yes. Now, have you finished with your comment so that I give the word to Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask the registrar to provide a tape for me because I'm absolutely sure that I did not put the question in the way I would say "armed soldiers," I simply wouldn't say something like that. But very well, the witness clarified that. The answer he gave is very clear on that. So this is something we can discuss later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair enough. I think it's a fair comment. If you need to hear the transcript -- not the transcript, sorry, the tape now, I think it can be arranged. It will be a matter of a few minutes and we can afford to wait because I think we have ample time on our hands this morning. So if you want to hear it now, we will do it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can do that after the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Ms. Sellers, please take account of what Madam Vidovic has said. And if you have further questions to the witness, direct them accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment. I still now have to -- and this is where I make mistakes. All right. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, you've heard us reading back your evidence from evidence. Now, I want to go back to my question. What had you heard about Ejub Golic that made you want to join his unit?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a unit, a group, because I knew the man from my municipality, from before the war, and because he was in the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the terminology group now as opposed to unit, and I would just want to clarify when you're speaking about group or your evidence, it clearly says "unit." Are you talking about fighters, men who carried weapons, and men who engaged in fighting? Is that what the group or unit that you're referring to did?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't consider them fighters. These were people who were there to defend Cizmici and Becirovo [phoen]. That was the only village that was at the entrance to Bratunac on the way to Srebrenica. So that village meant for us that a few more people could seek shelter in the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, if I am correct, the group defended the free territory and held the front line. Would you agree with that, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the front line. These were just people guarding these villages and they were in shelters, but the front line is waging war and actions and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you defending that territory in Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at this time you were able to have a weapon to assist you to defend the territory. Is that correct, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have weapons when I joined the group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic -- Madam Sellers. We'd like to know where Cizmici is, if perhaps the witness can indicate it on the map for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have the Defence map 727.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, I can lend you -- usher, you can have mine and all we need is for him to point it out. Thank you. It must be near Bratunac, no? Something like that? If it's not on the map -- I thought so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I clarify. Is it physically on the map or just too small, because as you explained yesterday some towns don't appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would it be further up from Bratunac? Is it outside this map, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the Bratunac area and it's close to Glogova, and I believe that that is not on the map at all. However, Mr. Tiro, would you please check. I think that that is quite far from the spot. I don't think the witness can see it. I don't think it's on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Is it a small village, Cizmici, or how big is it? Mr. Tiro can tell us. How big is the village of Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Cizmici had no more than 14 or 15 houses. It's a very small village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will ask the question again. I just want a confirmation of it. Why was it so important to defend Cizmici if it was only a village of 14 houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the only place to find shelter for the people from Bratunac and the surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, if it assists, Your Honour, we have a map where Cizmici does appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to see it, Judge Eser? No, it's okay. I thank you for your assistance, Madam Vidovic and Mr. Jones. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It does call up a lot of question marks. Like if you are defending a village of 14 houses, do you really need a unit? How big was this unit, if it was a unit? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to ask a couple more questions and we might want to see the Defence map that is larger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, then Cizmici is near the town of Glogova, and are you familiar that Glogova in May 1992 was the scene of action where Muslims were expelled?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that but I really couldn't cross into Glogova. There was no access to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the map that you have that is a bit inadequate for our purposes, would you agree that Glogova lies further to where I would be calling the north-east above Bratunac on this map. Is that correct? North-west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the direction of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, I was going to suggest isn't it in between Bratunac and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's in the valley, however. Right? And Jezestica and that area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Glogova is linked to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And are you familiar with any action done on the 24th of December, 1992, in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know it at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you become familiar with that in 1992 or did you become familiar with it after 1992? And then please tell the Trial Chamber what you mean by "I couldn't know it at that time."

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we had no access to Glogova and I didn't turn back to investigate what was going on at either Glogova or Kravica or any other Serb village. It was far from my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993, Mr. Tiro, after you'd gone to Kravica, did you then, when you'd joined the unit, come to understand the fighting that had taken place at Glogova and the villages in that area of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I joined the unit, or rather the group, because a unit cannot be made up of 30, 40, or 50 people. A unit means that you must have a battalion and a brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what qualification would you give your group in a military sense if "unit" is improper?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a group of people, a group of volunteers, that was set up to defend themselves, because not a unit. I mean, a unit can be in a division, a battalion, a brigade, whatever. Because now it would almost appear as if we had divisions of military strategists in Bratunac or Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge that didn't exist, right, military strategists or any type of formation of that extent. Would that be your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is unclear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Tiro. Let me try and rephrase that. From what you have just said that if you had a unit or a battalion, it would almost mean that we had strategists and that we didn't have that in Bratunac or Srebrenica, and I am paraphrasing a bit. So then I asked you that therefore, to your knowledge, what you knew, military strategists or types of formations such as brigades, battalions, did not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. exist in Srebrenica. That's what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I myself never knew about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just tell us then how many men were within your group or the group of Ejub Golic's men that you considered yourself a part of?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time I was there myself with them, between 40 and 50 people were defending that village, the locals from that village, and then from Glogova there was myself and my five cousins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these some of the cousins or relatives who had moved to Srebrenica with you in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of the summer of 1992, those who came to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by 1993 when you were within this group along with your -- some of your relatives, wasn't it true that Kravica was now within the hands of Muslim fighters, and that Glogova was also back within the hands of the Muslim population, and that that consisted of part of the line of defence, the territory of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself wouldn't be in a position to confirm that Kravica was in Muslim hands because those of us who were at Cizmici couldn't even get through because there was the demarcation or the division line between Cizmici and Glogova. And that territory was held by the Serb army from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then after December of 1992, are you saying that the Serb army held Glogova or am I misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You misunderstood, Madam. They held the territory of Zvijezda. That was the name of the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I ask the witness just to see our map P450 so we can be absolutely clear, and I'll move on from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I can get my map back. One of the things that you can -- whether he is aware at any time Glogova was recaptured or retaken by the Muslim -- by the Muslims, let me not use forces or whatever, whether he is aware of that and if he is aware of it, when according to him did it happen. Because I think it will clarify, help to clarify, a little bit the position at the moment which is to my mind a little bit unclear.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, you've heard Your Honour's questions. I wonder if you could answer them, if you're aware of when Glogova was in the hands of the Muslims and when did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when that would have happened because I was at Cizmici, but I don't know about Glogova having been in Muslim hands because otherwise there would have been people from Glogova there. People from Srebrenica would have had no need to go and defend Glogova. Because after Kravica everybody withdrew, the civilians withdrew to Srebrenica from Konjevic Polje and Cerska and Glogova. And they all withdrew, some in the direction of Srebrenica and others in the direction of Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were unaware in 1992 and 1993 that Ejub Golic was one of the fighters or heroes that had retaken Glogova for the Muslims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Madam. He wasn't a hero, he wasn't an outstanding fighter either, and he never took Glogova at the time when I joined his group of people because otherwise I would have been involved in that action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand. Could I just ask you to look at the map so that we can precisely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. In the meantime, let me hear Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we clarify. The witness gave a very clear answer to the fact that when he was at Glogova, Mr. Golic didn't take Glogova. And he did not refer to the period of time before he got to Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I understood it. When did you actually join Ejub Golic's group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As soon as I found the rifle at Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In January, mid-January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, your testimony was that you joined the group a couple days after you found the rifle in Kravica. So can I safely suggest that it was around mid-January 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please show us on the map that's provided in front of you where Cizmici is located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the map has to be moved in the direction of Kravica. Further up. We need -- no, Bratunac must go to the left side of the screen. No, that's going -- taking it to the right. Sorry. Yeah, yeah, yeah. It's the opposite. But it's not clear. I mean, I can't even distinguish one name on this map. I think I would rather -- I would rather rely on the map that Ms. Vidovic or Mr. Jones volunteered to us earlier on because I don't think that this is going to help us much. We need to move where Bratunac is to the right of the screen, please. I can't see it. I see Zvijezda but it should be near. Move it a little bit further to the right, please. Yeah, to the right, to the right, to the right, to the right. Now we see Jezestica, the Glogova Valley, and that is -- again further to the right, please. And it should be somewhere here where you see Siljkovici and -- Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm happy to put that on the ELMO. I just would ask for it not to be marked up because it's my copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course not. I mean, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm most grateful to our learned friends. I think it's just for illustration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I doubt whether it is on this map, I doubt it, because we are in the area definitely. Yes, there it is. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many kilometres is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Glogova --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- is Cizmici from Glogova, please? If you know, Mr. Tiro, could you inform us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if we could put down the map, further down, please, a little bit. No, no, that's further up. Okay. Thank you. So we'll get an idea of Bozici. All right. I thank you, and I thank you, Mr. Jones as well and Madam Vidovic of course. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tiro, I had asked you earlier in recounting your testimony that you said that you voluntarily joined Mr. Ejub Golic's unit or group and you could have joined any other. What other groups are you referring to that you could have joined at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the people meet, people who have arms -- well, they could have set up a group. It didn't matter whether it was myself or another person altogether. We could set up a group and go where we pleased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're talking about any other groups of defenders, if I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. As soon as you have a person defending their land, their part of that land, they can be considered as defenders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're speaking about any other groups that might have had persons in them who were armed in order to defend their land or their area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know of any other groups that had armed persons who were defending areas when you were in Srebrenica in 1992 or into the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't even interested in that in the course of 1992. I didn't find anything out about that and I didn't even know any people from Srebrenica because Srebrenica is quite a long way away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you were in Srebrenica in 1992, did you ever hear about Zulfo's men, for example, as a group? Or Akif Ustic's men?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo is not from Srebrenica, he is from Suceska. And I found out about Zulfo perhaps even after 1995. And that man called Akif, I never knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Tiro, what I'm trying to understand is that you referred in your testimony to other units, even if we allow that now your testimony has changed and you want to refer to other groups. What groups would you be speaking about?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There can be a group of any people, but it's not a unit. Because I'm trying to explain that I myself as soon as I had a rifle could have set up a group around me, a group of volunteers. We could have agreed to go to a certain part of the country to defend it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut this short, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry anymore about the word "unit" or whether any of these possible groups that may have existed were units or not. The question that is being referred to you is simply whether you were aware of any other groups of armed men or armed people at the same time or before or after you joined Ejub Golic's group. Were there -- because yesterday you said you choose -- you could have gone to other groups but you choose -- you chose Ejub Golic's one. The question that is being put to you: Which were the other groups that you knew of at the time? Forget units, we are not talking about units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I did not know the people from Srebrenica. Of course there were people who had rifles, and I could have gone up to any man, whether it was in Suceska or Potocari or perhaps Srebrenica or Cizmici. That means that there were groups of people, but I myself decided for Ejub Golic's group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not putting any further questions. It's your cross-examination, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just have one other -- a couple other questions in this area --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, Mr. Tiro, we're going to move on. You were asked around that same time in the direct examination about having contacts with Ejub Golic, and you answered that you had been in touch with him on several occasions. And then you were asked by Madam Vidovic: "Tell us, do you have any information about whether Mr. Ejub Golic and that group of people around him considered anybody in Srebrenica as their commander? Was it stated that there was a command in Srebrenica?" And you answered: "No." And then you were asked the question: "Was this command in Srebrenica mentioned at all to you in any way?" And you responded: "No." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. My question to you is: In 1992 when you lived or stayed in Srebrenica, did you have any knowledge of any command or command structures?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew of no command whatsoever, as I've told you. Everybody went to defend that part of the country and defend the people, protect the people, in their own way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a member of Ejub Golic's group or unit, you were unaware of any command structure that might be over Mr. Golic's head. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there's a possibility that Mr. Golic was under command but you just don't know about it. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that nobody could have issued orders to Ejub because he had his own principles and nobody could order him around or issue any orders or commands to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Tiro, I imagine you're talking about his principles of integrity and personality, but I'm asking about a possibility of military command. And I put it to you that you might not have been in a position to know who could have militarily command or give orders to Mr. Golic. Doesn't that possibility exist?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm giving clear answers to the fact that I myself never heard about it, never knew about it, and I believe that this man could not have been under anyone's command.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the witness be shown -- excuse me one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask that the witness be shown P158.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think you need any further the map that has been made available by Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No. I thank the Defence. I don't think we will be using it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, perhaps you can hand it back to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I understand that this is on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine. Once more, thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, would you please read the paper that's been placed in front of you. And I would particularly draw your attention to the date, the 24th of December, 1992, and where it says "order." And in the English translation that I have it says that the "Glogova Independent Battalion shall be formed of conscripts from the Glogova general area. "I hereby appoint Ejub Golic commander of the Glogova Independent Battalion. "This order is effective immediately and shall be effective until a new order is issued." And then it says "commander of the Srebrenica armed forces," and the name of Naser Oric. Now, were you aware of this particular command structure between Naser Oric and Ejub Golic when you were in Srebrenica or after you joined Mr. Golic's fighting men?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Because this could have been copied in 1995. This document could have been copied then. I saw Naser Oric in Srebrenica only once and that was when I worked at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tiro, it's because you've never seen this document before or because you only saw Naser Oric once that you're saying that this possibility does not exist?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not because I saw Naser Oric once or because I saw this document, because I've proven quite clearly that nobody was in a position to issue orders or command Ejub Golic because this group was not set up in Srebrenica but in Bratunac. And these are two different municipalities and nobody could issue orders to him in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one detail that Mr. Tiro said and it did not get into the transcript. He said these documents could have been copied by Serbs in fact in 1995. And we don't see it in the transcript. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, is Madam Vidovic correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Sellers. One thing: I don't -- Mr. Jones and Madam Vidovic, I don't want any comments or statements with regard to any of the documents that we may be seeing in the presence of the -- of the witness. All right. It's a question of -- you understand what I am referring to? If you need -- if you need to remark something to the Trial Chamber, please tell us so and we will do it in the absence of the witness. You understood me completely?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. This was just a correction for the transcript because we heard the witness say that word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was important. That's not what I mean. Ms. Sellers, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, just to make sure that I understand your point, it's because persons from different municipalities such as Mr. Golic from Bratunac and Mr. Oric from Srebrenica could not have any military -- intervening military structures; one couldn't command the other. That's your answer in terms of why you don't believe that this document speaks the truth. Right?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that Naser and Ejub could -- or Zulfo or Akif could have been in command. I mean, people were simply -- all of them doing their job, and I cannot say here this person was my commander or that person was my commander. Because I personally, when I joined this group I didn't consider Ejub to be a commander either. He couldn't make me go to defend this village of Cizmici if I didn't want to do it of my own free will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do agree that people from Bratunac municipality -- let me rephrase. Not people, that Muslims from Bratunac helped Muslims from the Srebrenica municipality during this time period in 1992 when they were being confronted by forces from Serbia and Serbian forces in their own territory. They did assist each other, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two municipalities that border on each other. And there were people from Bratunac who were in Srebrenica before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they helped each other, didn't they, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that they helped, but everybody went in their own way to defend the place. They had their families there. Some people went with just their bare hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And don't get me wrong, correctly so, they defended the territory together. That's all I'm asking you, Mr. Tiro, and I think with that you would agree. Right?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we were of help to Srebrenica because we were in Cizmici and that borders on the Srebrenica municipality. Therefore, we were of immediate help to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Tiro, I'd like to move into a slightly different area, and I'd like to take you back to August 1992. You've testified that you, your brother, your brother-in-law, and I believe Hamdija Hazic went back through the woods to gather food in our village. Now, I need to ask some questions about that, and I understand that that's a very difficult time period for you because injuries were sustained and your brother-in-law was killed. Would you please tell me whether at that time period in August 1992 that whether any of you had guns with you when you went back into what was essentially unsafe territory?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Weapons, no. Because had I had weapons at the time I would have joined some group of people immediately, had I had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understand you didn't have any weapon until you went into Kravica, but what about your brother, your brother-in-law, or the other man who was with you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony you testified that there was a horse. And I'd like to know: Did you take the horse from Srebrenica or did you come into possession of this horse after you had returned to your village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I took the horse from Srebrenica, and I can also give you the name of the person who I took it from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please give us the name of the person who gave you the horse for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a man; it was a woman. Abida Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your intention to take the horse I assume was for carrying food back to Srebrenica or was it just for the transport of you going to the village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was for food so that I could bring food to her as well - it was an elderly woman - as well as to my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now to your knowledge, did people often take horses with them when they were searching for food outside of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those days of course it was the easiest thing to take a horse through the woods to make it easier for yourself to carry the load.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were going back to Gornja Orlica, you testified that you were there for two days. And I'd like to understand, did it take you two days to get there or did you stay there for two days after arriving?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way to Orlica that was one day then a day in Orlica to gather, collect the food, and then the third day I came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't just go to Gornja Orlica, you also went to Ruljevici, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way back from Orlica I went to Ruljevici because it was closer that way to get to Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether Ruljevici was still a place where there were Serbs or weapons any danger that could be presented to unarmed men?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I was I didn't actually enter the village. This was a field at the entrance to the village and it was close to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was actually a shortcut through the woods. That's the reason you chose to go to Ruljevici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified about what happened when you and your brother-in-law and your brother and Hamdija were ambushed. When you were able to escape the next day, did you take the horse back to Srebrenica with you and the food?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't drag it with me because they had killed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just took the food with you. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even manage to get the food. However, during the night I managed to get the body of my brother-in-law out of there so that I could bury him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and you've testified to that in fulfilling your duties. I want to know: When you came back to Srebrenica, did you inform anyone of what had happened to your brother-in-law, your brother, yourself, and Hamdija? I'm not speaking about your family. Did you inform anyone, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. authorities or officials or tell other people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who would I inform when I wasn't even aware that there was any authority, and had there been any authority, what could they have done? The authorities didn't even dare go to their territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell any of the units that might be interested in defending those areas or the groups of people who were armed who were interested in defending, did you give them this knowledge that there were armed men that you had encountered?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing that I could tell groups of people. I entered the Srebrenica territory where I didn't know any people. There was nothing to say to anyone. It was just a pain that stayed with me and my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, that I understand but I need to ask a couple questions related to the incident. Well, there came a time when you were able to speak to your brother about what had happened. And I believe that you've testified that he had been captured and he was asked questions about what units were in Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection. The Prosecutor is interpreting the witness's testimony wrongly. He didn't say that he was questioned about which units existed in Bradjevina but who of the Muslims participated in the attack on Bradjevina, which is something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From what I remember, Ms. Vidovic is correct, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mind rephrasing the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, yes, the question would then be: Which Muslims participated in the attack on Bradjevina. You would agree with that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot give you the names of a thousand civilians. Out of them I only know Vekaz Husic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His -- I don't think he understood you. Let's take it one question after the other. Ms. Sellers would like to know -- Ms. Sellers would like to know from you when you spoke with your brother Mehmed whenever it was, what did he tell you he was questioned about when he was captured? What was he questioned about, as he told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, he was questioned about which people attacked Bradjevina and whether he participated in that with these people. They asked him who had killed Slavko Jovanovic. My brother perhaps didn't even know this Slavko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Sellers, then you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He did mention -- the name of some particular person. I don't know in which context exactly, but it seems that he mentioned the name of this person in connection with whatever happened in Bradjevina. Is that correct? Did I hear you mention the name of a particular person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can explain and then we can move to any further questions that you may have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, would you respond to Judge Agius and explain who was the person that you mentioned, Slavko Jovanovic. I believe that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's not -- let him answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Slavko Jovanovic, Stanisa Stevanovic asked about him, that he should tell him who killed Slavko Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tiro, you stated a couple minutes ago that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I am not dreaming. Did you -- I just saw it -- you asked the witness this question. "Mr. Tiro, yes the question then be: Which Muslims participated in the attack in Bradjevina. You would agree with that, would you?" And he said: "Well, I cannot give you the names of a thousand civilians. Out of them I only know Vekaz Husic." Did you mention that Vekaz Husic or something similar to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you finish that sentence or finish that statement, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe Your Honour would like you to finish the statement about Vekaz Husic. You were about to say something about him?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, could I just ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's just that I don't like to have an unfinished statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, wasn't it Vehid Husic who gave you the information about the attack in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, it's not Vehid, it's Vekaz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vekaz?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not the first time Ms. Sellers has mispronounced the names of places and people, and she's not the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us whether that prior to -- well, the information you received about the attack in Bradjevina came from Vekaz Husic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Vekaz Husic, because he was in that group of people who went to Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Because you were not at Bradjevina yourself. You physically were not there. Right?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And when you were asked the question by Mrs. -- Madam Vidovic in reference to Mr. Husic: "What did he tell you what really took place?" You answered: "He told me that a group of people assembled with rifles headed by Vekaz Husic as well as thousands of civilians and that Bradjevina was exiled." We later on explained that terminology. But you said that a group of people assembled with rifles headed by Mr. Husic as well as thousands of civilians. That was your testimony. Remember, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge where did Mr. Husic come from, what town did he come from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vekaz Husic is from Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether he had any type of village guards, group of armed men, or a unit with him in Bradjevina? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards were around Mocevici without rifles. People went unarmed with their bare hands just to make sure that nobody would attack. So people did go there even without rifles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the Prosecutor perhaps could put the questions a little more clearly because she asked, at least that's how it was translated into Bosnian, whether Vekaz Husic had a group of people in Bradjevina and this is something that would confuse the witness. He is talking about Vekaz Husic and Mocevici and then it might seem as if this witness is not credible. I mean, the questions are simply not clear; they're not understandable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or they are not being interpreted maybe clearly sometimes. But I don't know, I'm not in a position because -- to say anything because I'm not following the interpretation in Bosnian of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, let me just rephrase that question, although --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks for telling us that. I mean, if the -- your question was interpreted the way that Madam Vidovic explained, then obviously it was interpreted in the wrong manner. Because that's not what I have in the transcript anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply, did Mr. Husic did tell you that he had any type of village guards or groups of armed men or unit with him in Bradjevina during the attack? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't have a guard in Bradjevina when the Serbs were in Bradjevina at the time. He could have had a guard of his own around Mocevici with people who had weapons and were without weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but now the question was very clear. During the attack. The question that you are being asked to answer is whether you were told by this individual, by Husic, that -- whether he had any armed persons, description that Madam Vidovic -- that Madam Sellers said -- used -- during the attack on Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. People could not have driven people out with their bare hands. There was a small group of people with Husic. I explained that to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I think that clears --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that's much clearer. I understand your evidence. Now, do you know a man named Dzevad Salkic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that man. I don't know where he's from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, am I correct then in understanding that the information that you received concerning any armed people at the attack on Bradjevina then came from Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attack on Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from Husic. I found out about it only from Husic, from no one else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Husic acted together with the group of armed men that he told you about - that was your understanding - and then there were civilians in addition to it? I just want to make sure I'm completely clear on what you've testified about.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic acted together with the group of armed people and with the civilians in Bradjevina. That's my question. Is that your understanding of what Mr. Husic told you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And as a result of that the Serbs were driven out, exiled, removed from Bradjevina. That's what you understood Mr. Husic to say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there's a possibility that there was other information concerning civilians or these armed people that Mr. Husic was unable to or didn't or forgot to tell you about the attack on Bradjevina. Isn't that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. possible?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I personally wasn't interested in talking to people about attacks. All I wanted to do was to survive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- answers your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, it doesn't. I will try and rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, in the meantime let me hear what Mr. Jones --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I point something out in the transcript. Possibly it's a question of how the question has been put. The question initially was: So Mr. Husic acted together with the group of armed men that he told you about, so Husic acting with a group of armed men. When the question was put again, it was Mr. Husic acted together with a group of armed men and with the civilians. Now, I take it from the way the question was put initially that it's Husic together with a group of armed men, not acting together with civilians. But the way the sentence -- the question was rephrased the second time it suggests that he was -- the group was acting together with civilians, and that was not how the question was put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I intentionally rephrased the question to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I can understand why you -- of course and I understood at the time why you had rephrased the question. But perhaps we could clarify this and also this last part which according to me he answered in a way that does not respond to your question. Let's start with this last one. You were asked, Mr. Tiro, by

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: "So there is a possibility that there was other information concerning civilians or these armed people that Mr. Husic was unable or didn't -- or forgot to tell you about the attack on Bradjevina. Isn't that possible?" I will rephrase the question myself, not because it's not clear, don't misunderstand me, Ms. Sellers, but I will rephrase it my own way. I put it to you that what -- the information that Mr. Husic gave you about the attack on Bradjevina may not be complete, that he only gave you some information but not all information about that attack, would you accept it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only some things he told me, that the attack that would place, many civilians were killed, that he actually spread it around so that people find -- found out more about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. That, I think, answers that last question that you put. The other thing that -- once it has been mentioned now I think we need to clear it. When Mr. Husic was giving you information on the attack on Bradjevina, did he mention at all the presence during the attack of civilians, which I take it he did? And if he did, in what context did he mention civilians as being present during the attack on Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Civilians were present with Husic because they had had too much of shelling and shooting. And that's why the civilians also went to drive the Serbs out of that village, to make the situation easier for their own village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will not pursue it myself any further. I think it answers the questions that you put on both issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, it has, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you, of course, want to pursue the matter any further yourself, I suggest you do it immediately after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a 30-minute break starting from now. Do you think you will still finish by the end of the second session?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. I do not believe I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's what I thought. We will have a 30-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, we're going to continue in our -- continue our question-and-answer session now. I would like to just slightly shift to another area where you've mentioned the name Vekaz Husic. Now, am I correct that you testified that Mr. Husic also told you about the attack that occurred in Stanatovici? Let me try and further mispronounce the name or maybe pronounce it correctly, because I do not mean to confuse you. Stanatovici. Do you understand what I'm trying to say, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please assist me then.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Certainly. Because I said clearly that the Stanatovici people withdraw of their own accord and they torched the village in order to prevent us from getting the food or anything else for that matter. That's what Mr. Husic told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just to make it clear. When -- we're referring to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tiro, did you get any other information from Mr. Husic about that attack or what occurred there or was he the sole source of your information?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's divide it into two questions, Ms. Sellers. Did you receive information, other information, on the attack on Stanatovici from anyone else apart from Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, not even Husic went there when he saw that everything had burnt down. There was no need for him to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, that wasn't the question. Did anyone else, apart from Mr. Husic, give you information on what happened at Stanatovici, or Stanatovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm giving a proper answer. Husic was the only one who gave me this piece of information, that is to say, that Stanatovici had been torched and that there was no action whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That answers that part of the question. Now, the other thing is this: You have told us so far what Mr. Husic told you about the attack on Stanatovici. Did he tell you anything else on that event that you haven't told us as yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that answers your two questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if you want to pursue the matter of course you're free because I took over when you should be doing the -- yes, Judge Brydensholt would like to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: But was there at all an attack from the Muslim on this Serb village before the Serbs torched it? Was there an attack at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, because there are no Muslim villages in the vicinity either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, would you allow for the possibility that there was other information concerning this incident that you just weren't told and therefore were not aware of?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't even interested in finding out anything like that. And as to what went on amongst themselves, they could not reveal their secrets to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Did Mr. Husic tell you who he received the information from since he wasn't physically present himself?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me who he got the information from, but it was sufficient for him to be able to follow what was going on in those Serb villages from Mocevici, that is to say, where there was fire and all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And one other question. If I understand correctly, you were not present during any of the fighting or action in Ratkovici. Could you just confirm that for me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which place, if you could repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm talking about now Ratkovici, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can confirm that. I wasn't there at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand during that time period you had very important family concerns that kept you close to home. That was your testimony, right, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say I was at home. I had my family with me and my mother was ill, and we were in the forest, outdoors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And your mother was quite -- was becoming ill at this point and it's among the reasons that your evidence was that you were not at Ratkovici and in addition you did not have a weapon, if I understood correctly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Tiro, would you allow for the possibility that there were persons who were armed other than the persons with Mr. Husic at Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because I didn't see it. I can only confirm that in relation to this smaller group with Vekaz Husic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Tiro, do you know whether the person that you referred to as Naser Oric was someone who participated in fighting or had groups who participated in fighting under his command or control?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. It has to be specified what fights, what fighting we're talking about. Is Ratkovici what is meant or I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you referring to any particular action?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Not at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I took it that you were not at this moment. So please answer the question. I think it's a case of repeating your question, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I asked you whether the person you referred to as Naser Oric was someone who participated in fighting, whether you knew that, or had groups who participated in fighting under his command and control?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with any such groups participating anywhere. All I know is that Naser Oric participated in the defence of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, would it be possible then that Naser Oric would have information concerning the defence in the area of Potocari or in the Srebrenica municipality? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I'm feeling very uncomfortable with the question itself -- myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Should I withdraw it, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hear what Ms. Vidovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. It was pure speculation. Basically the witness is asked to make assumptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not really. I mean, the question is: Would it follow that because of what you said he would be in a position to know what happened in Potocari? But at the same time, what's the use of asking this question? I mean, you cannot force Mr. Oric to come forward and give us the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly not, Your Honour. But, Your Honour, if you would just bear with me one minute, I'm asking Mr. Tiro:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then would you agree Mr. Oric might be someone knowledgeable. Since you have testified that he participated in the defence of Potocari, would he be someone who might have been -- would be knowledgeable about the defence of Potocari or the larger Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't in a position to know everything. He would be a general in the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It didn't mean that he had to know everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is your answer yes or no, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he would not be in a position to know about -- to be knowledge able about defending Potocari or Srebrenica. That's your answer?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my own experience, he did not have to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Mr. Tiro be shown Prosecution Exhibit P90.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it on Sanction?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, it is on Sanction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That would spare us having -- because we have got six volumes here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to refer to page 89 eventually, but I just want to make sure first that we see the title page of Prosecution Exhibit P90. And it's Srebrenica -- excuse me. "Srebrenica Testifies and Accuses Genocide of Bosnia, Eastern Bosnia." And it is a book that the Prosecution understands is written by Mr. Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm going to go to page 89 in the English translation. The ERN number, and it should have the equivalent for B/C/S, would be 00816759.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a book that the Prosecution has submitted to us on a number of occasions in a number of different versions with different numbers. And now we're being told a number that we don't have. Could you give us the page number in the Bosniak version because this is the reason why I've brought the book along. And please, Your Honours, I think that this is something that can't have an impact on the witness's testimony, but I really think that it is unfair for any exhibits to be submitted to us in this way because this makes it impossible for me to prepare for the extra questions and I simply can't follow what the Prosecution is trying to say, and it is important because of the translation as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. First of all, I mean, does this book exist in our records under different exhibit numbers or --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the first thing we need to establish.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I believe this has only been referred to as Prosecution Exhibit 90, P90.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that conflicts with what you have just told us, Ms. Vidovic, and I want to clear this up because it's either P90 or it's also something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you allow me to consult with my case manager, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because this is something that needs to be established.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, if it is P90 could we be told what the page is in the original Bosniak version from the Exhibit P90.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Which page from the original -- I mean from the book itself are you referring the witness to?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because in the English version it's page 89, that much you told us. But you haven't told us, or at least I did not catch up the page number in the book itself. I mean, in other words, what is the witness being shown?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, could you just bear with me one second?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would beg the Court's indulgence. We'll move on to another topic to be assured of getting the correct page number. I understand Madam Vidovic's point and I have been using the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So could I ask that the exhibit be removed from the witness for the moment and we will come back to that when we have the proper information for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's move to something else, another document. Thank you, Madam Vidovic, for raising the matter. I think it needed to be raised.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And also please, I take it now that there is or seems to be in agreement there is only one document, which is this book. But please verify that once the matter has been raised. I want to be sure that this book is -- exists in our records as P90 and is also not some other number. I mean, that needs to be verified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
