utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just been advised that this is P90 and the book is not found under any other exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I see that the registrar is also confirming that for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but I need unanimous consent on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, thank you for your patience. I would like to now move on and ask you a question that Mr. Husic is someone who you spoke with on occasion and who gave you information about events, particularly tension and fighting, in your area in 1992, April through July. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't have to mean that all the information I got was from Husic. Some things I could have observed myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. I'm just confirming Mr. Husic certainly was one of your sources of information and it's possible that you could observe things yourself. So we're in agreement. My question is: At times didn't you also receive information from Stojan Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the way things should be explained. Stevan Stojanovic gave out information about the Serbs arming themselves, but he could not tell me, okay, this is where an attack is going to take place, this is where war is going to be, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I completely agree with Mr. Tiro. As a matter of fact, the point that I wanted to make is that he referred to Mr. Stevanovic as a great friend, someone who is actually aiding and assisting the Muslim population and particularly telling you information. That's my point. And you agree with that, don't you, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree that we got this information from him in as far as the Serbs getting arms were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that since he was a good friend, he was a good man?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a very good man, and he was a good friend to my entire village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether Mr. Stevanovic -- Stojanovic, Mr. Stojanovic, was he alive toward the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself didn't see him again since the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he died during 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just told by the brother that he himself was killed in Bradjevina. And that's what his cousin Stanisa told me when he came to say hello to me and I didn't want to shake hands with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was he killed in Bradjevina at the same time Mr. Husic was in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because I did not get that information. And I wasn't a journalist either to go and take anything or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, I understand that. Could you tell the Trial Chamber, was Mr. Stevanovic -- Stojanovic a young man or an older man? Was he fighting age? That's what I'd like to ask.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honours, it is not Stojanovic, it is Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an elderly man, an elderly man. He must have been 55 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Husic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That makes us feel very old. If 55 is -- it's -- I start shivering.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's the witness's characterisation of the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 60 years young he says.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]

utterances.text: Did he ever mention to you in your conversations from June 1992 onward anything that happened to your good friend?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]

utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Tiro. I understand this might have been a difficult subject to speak about. Now I'd like to ask you: Did you ever come to know that Vekaz Husic became a commander or a leader of a group or a unit from Mocevici after June 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a leader or a commander, well, nobody actually acknowledged anything like that. It could only have been based on an agreement amongst the people. utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you testifying that Mr. Husic did not become any type of leader of an armed group or unit? Is that what you're testifying to right now?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have been like a leader, but he didn't stand out from amongst 15 or 20 people. But also I guaranteed that this was not the case in Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, just one last question about Mr. Vekaz. I'm trying to draw your attention to later 1992 and 1993. Did you have knowledge then that he became or he was a leader of an armed group or unit? Just yes or no, did you have that information or not about your friend?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have now been given the indication in the book where we can look, and if I can just turn back to that evidence. Would you please present him with P90 also.

utterances.text: Now, I'm informed that page 89 in the Bosnian version will be at number 02919375. It starts at page 157. Do you see where I'm reading from, sir?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could we have just some assistance from the usher to make sure that -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that he's got the correct page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm reading from a page with a subtitle, so that page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I would take it that he should be looking at page with ERN -- it must be the one before 02919375. There must be a subtitle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you just confirm for us there is a subtitle on that page?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would ask that you -- at least in the English version we turn the page, we would be on page 89 in the English version. And could you please turn the page, sir, and we're just a little bit more than midway down on the following page. There is a paragraph midway down that begins with: "Between 21 and 26 June, daily battles were fought to create a link that would go from the Skenderovici area to Osmaci to Poznanovici." Sir, do you see where I'm reading? That should be ERN that ends in 9375. Sir, do you see where I'm reading almost midway down through the page? The paragraph beginning: "Between 21 and 26 June." Thank you. Would you just say yes so that we pick that up from the interpreters, Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not hear what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tiro, could you repeat what you said, please, what you've just said, because the interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I just said that I saw this part of the book here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Tiro, I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the problem, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, that I have to react but perhaps the witness would be confused. In the book or it could be a wrong translation. utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That does make a difference. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It does make a difference to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And not to the witness, because the witness is looking at the page where supposedly it says: "Between 21st and 29th of June."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So your question should include both dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Then I will use a date as my learned friend has suggested between --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not seeing it because I only have the English version here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that Madam Vidovic knows exactly what she is saying. So your question should be directed to the period 21st to 29th of June and not the 21st to 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.text: So, Mr. Tiro, in that first sentence we'll have between the 21st and 29th of June, I believe that's what you're looking at. Please forgive my pronunciation. Now, looking at that sentence, and keeping in mind how you testified earlier, do you allow for the possibility that Naser Oric might have had information about forces, Muslim forces, who counter-attacked and liberated territory, including Ratkovici and Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know what kind of information he received and from whom he received it. This is the first time that I am seeing this book and regarding this book practically the whole of the Drina Valley was liberated. Where did so many people come from in order to liberate so many villages? Then in that case we would have been also in Bratunac and right to the -- next to the Drina with all of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I understand that your question calls for conjecture, but my question was: Do you admit the possibility then that Naser Oric had the information concerning our forces attacking -- counter-attacking and liberating Ratkovici and Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I personally think that he did not have this information and all of this was written just like that. utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to move on to the following page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe it's the following page also in the Bosnian version. It should therefore end in 377. utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll continue that sentence where it says: "Among the battles waged in July 1992, special mention should be made of the liberation of Likare on 2 July and the conquest of the positions," and among those positions the third position says "Stanatovici." Do you see that, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you allow that there might -- that Naser Oric might have information or knowledge that Stanatovici were part of the positions that were conquered or there was a conquest, a Muslim conquest in July of 1992?

utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.text: Yes, sorry, Your Honour. I'm objecting because I'm following the English where my colleague is following the Bosnian. There's an ambiguity there. utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, I would really ask that what counsel said be objected to. He's testifying, informing the witness of possibly his opinion of the authorship of the book, and I would really ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, put the question again, please, maybe --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because you've heard Mr. Jones, you know exactly what his problem was or is, so --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is that Naser Oric might have knowledge that the conquest liberation occurred in July 1992 of these positions, including Stanatovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stanatovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Stanatovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what kind of information he would when it was very hard to get to Srebrenica even through the woods. And Stanatovici are about 70 kilometres from Srebrenica, if not even more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is you don't know. Is that correct, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No what? No what? You mean you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's impossible for Naser to find out information about Stanatovici from such a distance, and there are many Serb villages in between Srebrenica and Stanatovici for this information to be conveyed to him. This book is not true at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers, I was going to ask another question, but I think I will stop here for the time being and you again take over.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. I would ask now that P90 be removed from Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tiro, for looking at these passages with us. Mr. Tiro, I'd like to turn your attention now to October of 1992. And you testified in direct examination about Fakovici. Now, Mr. Tiro, concerning Fakovici was this a town that you were familiar with that you had gone to many times prior to the war? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I believe you testified that you were on your way to Fakovici one day to get flour but never ended up arriving in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I never ended up arriving, but that I just couldn't really get into Fakovici. I did get to the outskirts of Fakovici though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And is it my understanding then that you were not present or never were able to get into Fakovici between May 1992 up until October 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get to the centre of Fakovici in October either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then is it more correct to say that from May 1992 through until the end of 1992, you were not physically present in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've testified also that there were two underage boys who were taken to Fakovici and who told you what was happening in Fakovici in the spring of 1992. That was your testimony. Now, were those two underage boys taken by police officers?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they taken to a police station as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken to the newly formed Serb police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then I'm correct in assuming that they were not taken to a command station or a command post of the military?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was their command, the command of the reserve forces of the police and of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does a command station mean to you so that I can just be clear in understanding your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the formation, the forming of the Serb national command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that with the two underage boys related to you after they had been released?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They only said that they were there at the command. We knew from before that they were forming their own Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your information concerning the Fakovici command is based primarily on knowledge before the two underage boys went to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, let's rephrase it. Did you know of the existence of this Serb Fakovici command before these kids, these children, were taken to it? Were you aware of its existence already or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Does that answer your question, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, what I'm trying to distinguish is was he referring --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know, but I'm trying to make things easier for you and for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tiro, after the two children, the young boys, returned you were not present in Fakovici to determine what they meant by "command station"?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally wasn't in Fakovici, but it is sufficient proof for me that Zoran Jovanovic and Petko Jovanovic came to me to tell our population that they were forming a Serb police command in Fakovici and that they were forming a new Serb municipality or they were forming a new municipality in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. And it's from the formation of the police and the Serb municipality, those authorities, from which you determined that that was a command station?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't conclude anything on the basis of that, but they personally told us that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tiro. Thank you for assisting me in understanding. So on October 5th when you went toward Fakovici, was it to fight or was it to gather food?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to fire from my rucksack. I didn't have a rifle. Of course I went to get food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the only thing that you were carrying was your rucksack. Is that what I understand?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had testified earlier that someone would put a rucksack on their back and others would just follow them because they knew that they were going toward food. Did you just follow someone with a rucksack toward Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that my cousins came that day and that I was working and that we set out that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to Fakovici with your cousins, and I assume they only had rucksacks. And it was just to get food on the evening in October. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tiro, why did you stop before going into Fakovici? Why didn't you go and get food?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how could I fall into the hands of their command and risk my life, hand myself over practically to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just to clarify, could Ms. Sellers repeat her question because I believe that the question was not properly translated. I had the impression that Ms. Sellers asked a question that referred to that particular occasion, and it was translated as: Why didn't he go earlier to Fakovici, before these events. So I think again that there is a difference between the question and the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What Madam Vidovic has just said, assuming that it is correct, would not reflect the question that you put as it appears on -- on the monitor, at least in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, I thought the answer made perfect sense but I'll certainly give a specific time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if he answered you with reference to a previous -- why he never went previously, well, I mean, that's a completely different answer to what we have here. Because if we read the transcript here, that reply, that answer, would not be to the question that appears here but to the question that Ms. Sellers -- Ms. Vidovic pointed out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, on the occasion in October when you and your relatives were going to Fakovici, my question is: Why did you stop and not go into Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stopped. I couldn't get in because of the shelling and the shooting. I didn't want to take any risks. That's why I found the food on the outskirts of a house -- at a house on the outskirts of the place, and I took the food and returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you arrive to these outskirts? What time of day did you arrive to these outskirts?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived around midday on the 6th -- no, actually on the 7th. On the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tiro, you've testified and confirmed a couple times that you didn't have any weapons. Now --

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that you were asked by Madam Vidovic during the direct examination whether you turned over your rifles to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLER
utterances.text: Let me go back to that part of the transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One -- is it about the transcript or --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we could have the transcript reference to which the Prosecutor is referring. When we ask the question, we provide the references and that helps. But I wasn't talking about rifles, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm about to give the reference, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm talking -- I'm referring to page 59 of the transcript from -- I'll just get your -- on the 5th of September. And I'm down at line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- because I have to go to the page. 50 -- 59?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Line 22. "Who were the people who had those rifles?"

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, Your Honour, line 23. In my transcript it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Razim Sezanovic [phoen] he had the automatic rifle because he was the active policeman, and the other person was Sevel Husic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm on a different line. Your Honour, my line 23 reads: Did you turn over the two rifles you had to the Serbs on that occasion?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we are not fine-tuned. Is it page 59?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: For me it's page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you read it again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm on page 59, of my transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And there is the question Madam Vidovic asked: "Did you turn over the two rifles you had to the Serbs in relation to that ultimatum?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I have an answer that says "no."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mine it is page 60, line 7 and 8. And the answer is on page -- on line 9. It's okay. I mean, it's no big deal. The important thing is that I can follow you.

utterances.text: So, Mr. Tiro, you've given evidence, you've testified --

utterances.text: I want to make sure. One moment, because I want to make sure that Mr. Jones and Madam Vidovic can follow you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES

utterances.text: Because if my record does not tally with theirs, I have to assume or I will make sure about your record.

utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that the witness could testify about it but I don't believe that Mr. Jones --

utterances.text: All right. Just read out from that transcript whatever you need to read out to the witness and then put your question, please.

utterances.text: Your Honour, right now I'm going to withdraw the question. I believe that the comment that has been made by Defence counsel concerning the question and concerning the comments and the content --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, point taken and question withdrawn. Let's move to the next.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.text: Now, one moment because I have to get this out. Yeah, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. One moment because now I am on the 6th. 7th. All right. Okay. All right. Go ahead.
